texts.facts: 1) By this Petition filed by Central Railway, exception is taken to the Award passed by the Central Government Industrial Tribunal No. II, Mumbai (CGIT) by which the Tribunal has answered the Reference made on behalf of Respondent-Union in the affirmative and has directed P e t i t i o n e r - C e n t r a l R a i l w a y t o t r e a t t h e e m p l o y e e s i n v o l v e d i n t h e _______________________________________________________________________________ Friday, 17 October 2025 Neeta Sawant WP-576-2007-FC Reference as its employees and regularise them on the work on which they were working with the consequential benefits. 2) City of Navi Mumbai has been planned, designed, and developed by City and Industrial Development of Corporation of Maharashtra Limited (CIDCO), which is a New Town Development Authority and also a Planning Authority under the provisions of Section 113 of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966. As a part of development of planned city of Navi Mumbai and to provide faster connectivity to Mumbai City, a railway line was planned to be laid. CIDCO is the land owner in the entire city of Navi Mumbai as the State Government has acquired land and handed it over to CIDCO. Ordinarily, it is a function of Railways to construct railway stations after General Manger, Central Railway vs The Secretary, Rail Mazdoor Union on 17 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18681859/ 1 laying of railway lines. However, in the present case, a unique arrangement was made where CIDCO constructed world class railway stations in the city of Navi Mumbai at Vashi, Sanpada, Jui Nagar and Belapur. As opposed to a usual railway station providing necessary infrastructure for boarding and alighting from trains, CIDCO envisaged construction of railway station complexes including commercial offices, food courts, restaurants, etc for non-railway purposes. To illustrate, a commercial complex has been built by CIDCO at Vashi Railway Station which houses International Infotech Park. On similar lines, other railway stations have been constructed by CIDCO at various other points within the city of Navi Mumbai. 3) Since CIDCO was associated with construction of railway stations, it also decided to maintain t h e m , r a t h e r t h a n l e t t i n g R a i l w a y s t o _______________________________________________________________________________ Friday, 17 October 2025 Neeta Sawant WP-576-2007-FC maintain the otherwise swanky railway stations. Accordingly, an Agreement was executed between CIDCO and Central Railway on 1 August 1998 under which CIDCO took the responsibility of maintaining the railway stations, food court areas, offices of Central Railway Administration etc. In return, Railways granted advertisement rights to CIDCO to recoup the expenses incurred towards maintenance of the railway stations. 4) According to the Petitioner-Central Railway, CIDCO employed various workers for discharging its obligations under the Agreement dated 1 August 1998 for maintenance of the railway stations. By letter dated 22 April 1999, Respondent-Union wrote to Regional Labour Commissioner (Central), raising a dispute relating to 37 workers deployed by CIDCO at various railway stations and sought for regularization of their services into railways on the ground of completion of 240 days of service. By order dated 24 May 2000, Government of India, Ministry of Labour referred the dispute for adjudication to CGIT. The Schedule of the reference reads thus : THE SCHEDULE "Whether the Action of the Management of Central Railway, Mumbai, by not regularizing the Services of 37 Workmen (Listed in Appendix 'A') working continuously in the Cleaning, Sweeping, etc., for the last more than four years at the Various Railway Stations of Navi Mumbai is justified? If not, what Relief, the Workmen are entitled to?" 5) The Union filed its Statement of Claim, in which it was clarified that only 15 out of t h e 3 7 w o r k e r s w e r e i n t e r e s t e d i n p r o s e c u t i n g _______________________________________________________________________________ Friday, 17 October 2025 Neeta Sawant WP-576-2007-FC the Reference, whose names were indicated in para-2 of the Statement of Claim. The claim of the Respondent-Union was resisted by Central Railway by filing Written Statement. The Respondent-Union filed Rejoinder. The Respondent-Union led evidence of various workers and of General Secretary of the Union. The Petitioner apparently did not lead any evidence. The CGIT has rendered Award dated 31 May 2006 allowing the Reference and directed the Petitioner to treat the employees involved in the Reference as its employees and to regularise their services by grant of benefits. Petitioner is aggrieved by the Award dated 31 May 2006 and has filed the present General Manger, Central Railway vs The Secretary, Rail Mazdoor Union on 17 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18681859/ 2 Petition. By order dated 28 March 2007, the Petition has been admitted. However, it appears that no interim relief is granted in favour of the Petitioner. The Petition was dismissed for non- prosecution on 12 June 2017, which has been restored by order dated 24 November 2017 by imposing costs of Rs.10,000/- paid to the Respondent-Union. The Petition is called out for final hearing.
texts.arguments: 6) Ms. Smita Thakur the learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner would submit that the CGIT has erred in granting the relief of regularisation to the workers of CIDCO on the establishment of Central Railway. That the concerned workers are not employed by Railways in any manner. That Railways has not paid salaries or wages to them at any point of time. That Railways does not supervise their work nor take any decision in relation to their service conditions. She would submit that the impugned Award travels beyond the scope of Reference. That there was no reference about c o n t r a c t b e t w e e n C I D C O a n d R a i l w a y s b e i n g s h a m o r _______________________________________________________________________________ Friday, 17 October 2025 Neeta Sawant WP-576-2007-FC bogus. That therefore regularisation of services of workers of CIDCO is impermissible on establishment of the Central Railway. 7) Ms. Thakur would further submit that Notification dated 9 December 1976 which prohibited engagement of contract workers for cleaning and sweeping work has been [LEAKAGE_MASK] and [LEAKAGE_MASK] by Constitution Bench in Steel Authority of India Limited Versus. National Union Water Front Workers1. That neither CIDCO nor its agency-M/s. Man Power Services had obtained necessary license from Competent Authority under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 (CLRA Act). That therefore the finding of existence of Notification prohibiting engagement of contract labour recorded by Tribunal is erroneous. That if the contract is found to be sham or bogus, such contract is referrable to the agreement between CIDCO and M/s. Man Power Services and not the agreement between CIDCO and Central Railways. She would rely upon judgment of the Apex Court in Balwant Rai Saluja and another vs. Air India Limited and others 2 in support of her contention that none of the six tests prescribed by the Apex Court are satisfied in the present case. She also relies upon judgment of the Apex Court in Kirloskar Brothers Limited vs. Ramcharan and others3 in support of her contention that when there is no Notification under Section 10 of the CLRA Act and where it is not proved that the contract was sham or bogus, the question of directing principal employer to absorb or regularise the services of contract labours does not arise. In support, s h e w o u l d a l s o ( 2 0 0 1 ) 7 S C C 1 ( 2 0 1 4 ) 9 S C C 4 0 7 ( 2 0 2 3 ) 1 S C C 4 6 3 _______________________________________________________________________________ Friday, 17 October 2025 Neeta Sawant WP-576-2007-FC rely upon judgment of the Apex Court in International Airport Authority of India vs. International Air Cargo Workers' Union 4. She would also rely upon judgment of this Court in Airports Authority of India Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport vs. Indian Airport Employees' Union and Others5. 8) Ms. Thakur would rely upon judgment of Constitutional Bench in Secretary, State of Karnataka and other vs. Umadevi and others6 in support of her contention that regularisation of casual, temporary or ad- hoc workers is impermissible when their engagement is made without following General Manger, Central Railway vs The Secretary, Rail Mazdoor Union on 17 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18681859/ 3 process of selection and in absence of sanctioned vacancies. That apart from the engagements being made by CIDCO and not by Central Railway, the same are not done against any sanctioned vacant posts or after following due process of selection. That therefore mere length of service put in by the concerned workers cannot be a ground for regularising their services. 9) Ms. Thakur would further submit that even though some of the workers may have continued to work on the job of maintenance of railway stations of CIDCO even today, their wages are paid through contractors by CIDCO. She would rely on clarificatory letter dated 9 October 2025 by Senior Divisional Operations Manager certifying that Central Railway has not deployed any manpower for cleanliness and other related activities at stations maintained by CIDCO nor their wages (2009) 13 S C C 3 7 4 2 0 1 6 S C C O n l i n e B o m 2 1 6 8 ( 2 0 0 6 ) 4 S C C 1 _______________________________________________________________________________ Friday, 17 October 2025 Neeta Sawant WP-576-2007-FC are paid by Railways. She would pray for setting aside the impugned Award. 10) Per contra, Mr. Ramamurthy, the learned counsel appearing for Respondent-Union would oppose the Petition. He would submit at the very outset that out of total 37 workers on whose behalf Reference was initially made and out of 15 workers on whose behalf the Reference was prosecuted, only six workers continue to work as Safai Kamgar at railway stations. He would submit that they have been working since 1992-1995 and have thus rendered over 30 years of service and otherwise deserve to be regularised. He would submit that considering that the Petition involves regularisation of services of only six workers, the impugned Award be upheld by restricting its implementation only in respect of the six workers. 11) Mr. Ramamurthy would further submit that no interference is otherwise warranted in the impugned Award of the CGIT. That the Tribunal has rightly appreciated the position that the work of maintaining the railways stations is essentially that of Railways. That the activities which are required to be performed by Railways are getting performed by it through CIDCO. That though the wages are paid through CIDCO, the liability towards it is actually owned by Railways. That an arrangement is made under which Railways have permitted to exploit advertisement rights at the railway stations by CIDCO and this is how wages are indirectly paid by the Railways to the workers through CIDCO. He would submit that the essential test to be determined is about the entity for w h o m t h e w o r k e r s w o r k . S i n c e t h e r e i s n o d i s p u t e a b o u t l i a b i l i t y o f _______________________________________________________________________________ Friday, 17 October 2025 Neeta Sawant WP-576-2007-FC Railways to maintain their stations, the work performed by the workers is essentially for Railways. 12) Mr. Ramamurthy would further submit that the concerned workers have been engaged for working at railway stations right since construction thereof. By the time the Petition is filed, they had completed more than 15 years of service. That M/s. Man Power Services was associated with the workers only for initial three years during 1992 to 1995 whereafter there is direct employer-employee relationship between Railways and workers. That the work performed by the workers is of perennial nature. That Central Railway has not obtained any license to engage contract workers at their railway stations in Navi Mumbai. The services of the workers are continued even General Manger, Central Railway vs The Secretary, Rail Mazdoor Union on 17 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18681859/ 4 after expiry of tenure of agreement with CIDCO. That therefore the Tribunal has rightly granted the relief of regularisation to the workers. He would pray for dismissal of the Petition. 10. The Corporation shall maintain the said stations in the proper state of upkeep and r e p a i r a t i t s o w n c o s t f o r t h e p e r i o d o f f i v e y e a r s _______________________________________________________________________________ Friday, 17 October 2025 Neeta Sawant WP-576-2007-FC w.e.f. the date of signing of this agreement. In para-12 to 14 of the judgment in Kirloskar Brothers, it is held as under : 12. In the present case, neither any notification under Section 10(1) of CLRA Act has been issued prohibiting the contract labour, nor there are allegations and/or even findings that the contract is sham and bogus and/or camouflage. 13. In International Airport Authority of India v. International Air Cargo Workers' Union ((2009) 13 SCC 374) , after considering the decision of this Court in SAIL v. National Union Waterfront Workers ((2001) 7 SCC 1), it has been observed and held by this Court that where there is no abolition of contract labour under Section 10 of the CLRA Act, but the contract labour contends that the contract between _______________________________________________________________________________ Friday, 17 October 2025 Neeta Sawant WP-576-2007-FC the principal employer and the contractor is sham and nominal, the remedy is purely under the ID Act. It is further observed that the industrial adjudicator can grant the relief sought if it finds that the contract between the principal employer and the contractor is sham, nominal and merely a camouflage to deny employment benefits to the employee and that there is in fact a direct employment, by applying tests like: who pays the salary; who has the power to remove/dismiss from service or initiate disciplinary action; who can tell the employee the way in which the work should be done, in short, who has direct control over the employee. General Manger, Central Railway vs The Secretary, Rail Mazdoor Union on 17 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18681859/ 9 14. It is further observed that where there is no notification under Section 10 of the CLRA Act and where it is not proved in the industrial adjudication that the contract was a sham/nominal and camouflage, then the question of directing the principal employer to absorb or regularise the services of the contract labour does not arise. It has further been observed in paras 38 and 39 as under: ( International Airport Authority of India case, SCC p. 388) "38. The tests that are applied to find out whether a person is an employee or an independent contractor may not automatically apply in finding out whether the contract labour agreement is a sham, nominal and is a mere camouflage. For example, if the contract is for supply of labour, necessarily, the labour supplied by the contractor will work under the directions, supervision and control of the principal employer but that would not make the worker a direct employee of the principal employer, if the salary is paid by a contractor, if the right to regulate the employment is with the contractor, and the ultimate supervision and control lies with the contractor. 39. The principal employer only controls and directs the work to be done by a contract labour, when such labour is assigned/allotted/sent to him. In short, worker being the employee of the contractor, the ultimate supervision and control lies with the contractor as he decides where the employee will work and how long he will work and subject to what conditions. The primary control is with the contractor." In Balwant Rai Saluja (supra) the Apex Court has laid down six tests in para- 65 of the judgment as under : 65. Thus, it can be concluded that the relevant factors to be taken into consideration to establish an employer-employee relationship would include, inter alia: General Manger, Central Railway vs The Secretary, Rail Mazdoor Union on 17 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18681859/ 10 (i) who appoints the workers; (ii) who pays the salary/remuneration; (iii) who has the authority to dismiss; (iv) who can take disciplinary action; _______________________________________________________________________________ Friday, 17 October 2025 Neeta Sawant WP-576-2007-FC (v) whether there is continuity of service; and (vi) extent of control and supervision i.e. whether there exists complete control and supervision. General Manger, Central Railway vs The Secretary, Rail Mazdoor Union on 17 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18681859/ 11 25)
